author: Fable (brief 011; GDD v0.22.0 §04, §07, §09, §10, §14)
rule: The words of the Handover, made at build time and read by the Unity host; nothing here is written live and no line decides anything (GDD §09: text is a light layer, history is what the systems record). The host finds a line with lookup() and picks a variant with pickIndex() (contracts/missions/handover/text.schema.ts): same seed and same run, same words. Keys follow the engine: verbs are the panel verb ids, outcomes the rulebook outcomes (`suspicious` when the person reports the approach), refusals are text codes found by lockOf() because the engine returns free text. People are named only Inez and Vale; everyone else is a role. Civilians are never the payload: no line asks a civilian to die, fight or be used as a weapon. Lines that name Halcyon are pending Sky (a Story proposal): ship the `unnamed` cliffhanger until Sky decides. Inez and the door guard are lovers (the Story spine; Sky, 2026-10-15): her debt is her need (Help), her secret is the guard (Pressure threatens to expose it). Written plainly and with tact, never explicit.

tone.world: An alternate 1950s that found atomic power centuries ago: 1950s manners and speech, centuries-ahead machines, no thinking machines or networks. Optimistic on the surface, coercive underneath: the city is polite, orderly and watching. Speech is plain, short and spoken; no period slang to dress it up, no modern internet speech.

voices.scout: terse and observant: fragments, what is where, counts and positions; never warm, never wrong
voices.fixer: warm and persuasive: reassures, says "we", puts people at ease; steel under the kindness
voices.tech: calm and practical: procedure, minutes and what is tied to what; patient, a little dry about old wiring
voices.enforcer: dry, older, few words: one to four words where he can; gallows humour, never a speech
voices.waitress: Inez: warm café patter, quick, tired about money and the lender; her temperament shows in what she will and won't take
voices.driver: Vale's official driver: gruff and practical; cars, wages, schedules; calls Vale "the Councillor"
voices.guard: the door guard: officialese, clipped, the post and the rules; a mercenary one talks bonuses and "off the clock"
voices.councillor: Vale: formal and pompous, then frightened; loyal blusters, mercenary bargains, fearful begs
voices.rivals: cold and businesslike: a contract, a schedule, no names
voices.patrol: a clockwork patrol: fixed polite phrases that mean orders ("Walking is encouraged. Running is reported.")
voices.security: the response unit: crisp, loud, procedural
voices.watcher: a person in the camera room, speaking into a handset: reports what the camera shows
voices.crowd: passers-by: startled, short, human; they never fight and are never used

pick.rule: variant index for the n-th use (0-based) of a key in a run: for i = 0..n, at = fnv1a32(seed + "|" + key + "|" + i) mod count, and if at equals the previous use's variant (count > 1) then at = (at + 1) mod count. fnv1a32 is the rulebook's (contracts/rules/rulebook.ref.ts, 32-bit FNV-1a over the UTF-16 code units). The key is event/verb/speaker/outcome/temperament/about with absent parts skipped; `seed` is the run's seed string. The line is the entry lookup() finds: every field an entry names must equal the query's, the entry naming the most fields wins, file order breaks a tie.

briefing.title: The Handover
card: Councillor Vale signed the clearance order for the marked block.
At shift handover he leaves the Civic Records Office for his car.
We take him alive, get him into our getaway car and drive off.
Quietly, if we can. Others want him too, and this city notices noise.
We have $100,000, four people and until 8:30.

cards.rule: The feed's cards for engine events no scene covers (Sky's review 2026-10-16, messages.html §1 D). Each is a title and one result in the player's words with the engine's numbers, never the engine's sentence (its log keeps that). A card with `sight` shows only when an agent can see the place, as a city scene does. A result that is a record is chosen by the engine state `pick` names. {who} is the person or watcher as names.targets says it, {agent} "the Scout"; the host capitalises the first letter after filling. Brief 013 (takedowns): a card says only what the cell has seen or been told. Three kinds: (1) the cell's own acts (the agent is there, so no `sight`); (2) things at a place the cell may not be near: `sight` in-sight, and `at` names the engine position the check looks at (the log carries none; the host reads it from the game); (3) the city's answer to an Alert, which the Alert pill and the street show: a card says that it came and when, never who made the report or why. `needs` routine: a cause the cell can name only once a Watch has taught the person's routine (a missed check in); until then report.landed speaks alone. Codes the engine builds (stash.container, stash.door) are one card keyed by the prefix. A spoken line of an event shows with that event's card or scene, so it follows the same sight rule: a line is never shown when its card is hidden. Brief 014 (less reading): every card has a `fate`: beat (a one-line feed beat, `beat`; at most ten distinct lines in the file), icon (the street shows it: a marker, ring, lock or pip), alt (history only, behind L), debrief (the end says it). A card with no beat is never a card on screen; its title and result are the history lines.

rules.one: One at a time, in priority order, lowest number first (H14, H16 and H15, the end steps, are -4 to -2: they win over every other hint, H17 and H13 included, when their trigger holds; their triggers never hold together; H17, the fight hint, is -1, behind H15 so that Put Vale in the car wins while a fight holds the car, ahead of H13).

rules.idle: A hint shows only after the cell has given no order for 8 s.
rules.vanishes: It vanishes the moment its gone-when act happens, or when its trigger stops holding.
rules.words: Each line names an agent, a verb and a target, introduces one verb, and never names an approach, a time or a sequence.

less.rule: brief 014 (Sky, 2026-10-16: "It's the reading, it's too much"). The play HUD at rest shows no sentences: people speaking (bubbles in the world), icons, numbers, rings, and at most two story beats. Every long line elsewhere in this file stays and is the Alt text (hold Alt, or the history key L) or the debrief; nothing was deleted. `fates` says where each group of text goes; the rest of this block is the short forms and the one-line price grammar. Told/learned holds: a beat or a pop never names what the cell has not been told or has not learned.

price.rule: One line per way: the verb, then only the fields that are not zero, always in `order`; an unknown number is "?". Money is compact ($90k, $1.5k, a range $40k–60k; under $1,000 as it is): the rows have fixed columns; the status pill and the debrief keep whole dollars. Locked rows show the same line dimmed. Alt shows every field including the zeros, the walk split from the act, and the rows a card carries today (`actions.*.does`, found, never found, wakes, seen by).

name.shows: the verb's label, or its way (Knock out, Kill); the target is the card's header or the chip's lead icon

usd.shows: the cash the order spends, compact: $90k, $1.5k, under $1,000 as it is, or a range ($40k–60k) when the worst case is dearer; the status pill and the debrief keep whole dollars

time.shows: n s, the walk plus the act (Alt splits them)
time.hiddenWhen: the order lands at once (Call, Vale into the car)

alert.shows: the Alert mark and the Alert the order raises when it goes wrong (seen, reported, found, fired): 1, 3, or "≥2" for gunfire

eye.shows: the eye mark and who could see it: none, ? (a watcher the Scout has not learned could), or the watchers
eye.hiddenWhen: the order cannot be seen (a Call, a Watch from range)

learns.shows: the icons of what a Watch or Listen teaches: routine, sight, need, temperament

pace.shows: a carry's walking pace in m/s

mark.shows: the outcome mark: ✓ works, ✗ they would refuse, ½ not yet, ? unknown until the Scout has learned who they are
mark.hiddenWhen: the order has no answer to guess

feed.rule: The feed shows story beats only: a card's or a scene's `beat`, one short line each, and only when no bubble of that event's speech is on screen (say it where the player is looking: the person's own line if they are in view, else the beat). At most `maxOnScreen` at once, each gone after `seconds`, then it sits in the history (L). A beat identical to one shown in the last `dedupeSeconds` is dropped. A card with no `beat` is never on screen; its title and result are the history. The people in a scene speak as bubbles at the speaker: `bubblesAtOnce` at a time, `bubbleSeconds` each; overheard and approach scenes play every beat, call and city scenes their first `cityBeats`. A beat obeys the card's sight and needs rules (the cell is never told what it did not see).

objective.rule: The Next Objective is one imperative with the nouns that have a marker in [brackets], coloured as their markers. It shows for `showSeconds` when the clock starts, on each change (take, bring, carry) and when the pill's next mark passes (the chime, Vale's exit), then fades; the close (8:30) is on the clock pill. It never explains and it is not a hint.

steps.when: from the start, until the Enforcer is given Enter (routes A and G) or holds Vale (route B); and again if the Enter order is cancelled before the Enforcer is in
the Enforcer has an Enter order (walking to the door, or inside) and Vale is not yet with the Enforcer: shown at the order, kept while inside, replaced on coming out
Vale is with the Enforcer (out of the Office by Enter, or taken at the pickup by Take), until Vale is in the car
Vale is in the car (the Enforcer boarded with Vale) and no Go has been given, until the car leaves (brief 018)

briefing.rule: Before Begin the card shows the goal line, three numbers (close, purse, Alert) and the four portraits with their one-word roles. The sentences, the fails and the two ways in are Alt (B).

end.rule: The end card is one line, the tally (m:ss, $ spent, Trail) and two buttons. The sentence under it, the route, the security and investigation lines and Kept are the debrief.

alt.rule: The outcome marks in words, and what a Watch or Listen learns, for Alt. The host builds these by hand today (HudModel.OutcomeWords).

outcome.unk: ? until the Scout learns who they are
outcome.tethered: Loops the camera; the Tech stays at the cabinet

hint.rule: The Next Step is `hints.items.*.short`: one imperative, one [noun] ringed in the street and coloured as its ring, no agent named (the agent's portrait pulses with the verb icon at the line's left). It shows for `showSeconds`, fades to its ring, returns once after `returnSeconds` more of idling if still undone, and never shows more than `maxShows` times in a run. It retires for good, per profile, once the player has given the verb it teaches; the long `line` is Alt and the relearn key.

go.rule: Brief 018 (the getaway, section 6.5 and 6.6): the Go card and the roster flag. Nobody left: the card reads `none`. rules.what: Short scenes for the update feed (Sky, after playing): conversations between the people and the cell, overheard or played out, in the order of their beats. The log shows the first beat collapsed and all of them expanded; the result line is what the player now knows or has.

kinds.overheard: Watch or Listen lands: the target talks with the people around them (clerk, owner, customer, guard, driver). Watch learns the routine; Listen the need, the temperament and, for Inez, her secret.
kinds.approach: A turn order lands: the Fixer and the target, ending in the target's reply and the Fixer's reaction. Beats with `ref` are lines from `dialogue` (ack, arrive, reply, done, confirm), so a scene extends the exchange and never contradicts it.
kinds.call: The Fixer calls a turned contact: Inez calls the guard over and he leaves his post for her, with the coffee spill as cover; the driver parks across the pickup camera.
kinds.city: The city does something the cell may see. `sight` in-sight: show it only if an agent is within 13 m with a clear line; always: anyone hears it (the bell). Brief 013: a city scene may carry `outcome` (what the cell sees a witness do: report, flee, check) and `about` (the person missing); the host finds it with lookupScene() on the event, then the outcome.

rules.less: Brief 014: a scene plays as speech bubbles at the speakers, not as a card. Overheard and approach scenes play every beat (what the cell learns, and the Fixer's drama, are in them); call and city scenes their first `less.feed.cityBeats`. `result` is the Alt and history line; a `beat` is the one feed line when the scene starts.
rules.pick: A scene is found by lookupScene(); a variant is picked by pickIndex(seed, key, n, count); a `ref` beat is picked by pickLine() with the same seed and n.
rules.story: Inez and the door guard are lovers (the Story spine; Sky, 2026-10-15). The cell learns it by Listening at the café; he takes his café stop to see her, and when the turned Inez calls him over he leaves the door, which is what the call scene shows. Her debt is her need (Help clears it); the guard is her secret (Pressure threatens to expose it, and she resents it). Written plainly and with tact; nothing explicit.

items.title: Someone raises the alarm
items.result: A passer-by is calling it in. Alert will rise.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Look! There, by the wall!

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Is that someone lying there?

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Fetch the police! Run!

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: That's not right. That's not right.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Somebody hurt them. Look!

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: I'm calling it in. Now!

items.title: Someone freezes
items.result: A passer-by saw and is frightened. They may talk.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Oh no. Did you see that?

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Hush. I saw nothing. Nothing.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Walk. Just walk. Don't turn round.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Don't stare. Don't stare.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: They'll see us looking.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Go home. Say nothing. Please.

items.title: Someone stops to help
items.result: A passer-by is going to the body. They will find it.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Wait. Someone's down.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Careful. Is it a trick?

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Hello? Are you hurt?

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: That's a person down there.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: I'll look. Stay close.

beats.speaker: crowd
beats.line: Is anyone there? Wake up!
